name: preferences-readback-after-tool
description:
Regression for the mid-tool-loop preference-read bug. Within a SINGLE turn the agent reads preferences (get_preferences) BEFORE saving, so by the time set_preference runs there is already a tool_result turn in the transcript — stored role "user" (the LLM protocol models a tool result as a user-role message) with an EMPTY Author. set_preference's own readback then re-resolves the current user, and it must key off the human message turn, not that later tool_result, so it reports the value it just saved (source: user) rather than falling through to the class default.

resolvePreferencesTurnAuthor once took the highest-index user-role turn's Author unconditionally; a tool_result is role "user" with no Author, so mid-loop it resolved an empty author, skipped the user-scope read, and every preference read returned the default. In production the agent then believed the save had failed and re-prompted (the user approved the same save twice). preferences-save-and-recall never caught this: it recalls on a SEPARATE turn, where the latest user turn IS the human message (authored). This bundle keeps the read in the same turn as a prior tool call, which is the only shape that exercises the empty-author path.

Each user turn is more than one LLM step: after respond_to_user the runner makes one more model call carrying that tool's result, and only agent_work_complete ends the turn.
userTurns: check my current language setting, then set it to German

reply.text: Gespeichert — language is set to de.

args.summary: read current language, then saved German
